title: PLG Signal Outreach Cadence Templates v1 (Pilot) — Day 0/2/5/10
body:
Doc purpose
- Provide a consistent, low-spam outbound cadence for PLG-to-sales signals during the NA pilot.
- Use HubSpot Tasks + Templates (no sequencing tool in v1).
- Support multiple “why now” reasons: Scale/Spend, Reliability (429s / SLO pain), Compliance (SOC2/security docs/VPC intent), Team expansion (workspaces/invites).

Audience
- Primary: AEs + SDRs (pilot), SEs (when flagged), CS (existing customer expansions).

Operating principles (pilot)
1) Lead with the observed signal + ask permission to engage (avoid “we’re watching you” vibes).
2) One clear CTA per touch (15-min triage or 30-min technical deep dive).
3) Suppression > persistence: if nurture is running or CS already engaged, don’t pile on.
4) Focus on helping them succeed (capacity planning, rate limit strategy, security pack) rather than pitching plans.

Signal → cadence selection (quick chooser)
A) Scale / spend velocity
- Examples: sustained token growth, rapid spend velocity, growth trend across last 7–14 days.
- Goal: Offer Dedicated (predictable throughput, lower unit cost) + optimization consult.

B) Reliability / performance
- Examples: repeated 429s, elevated tail latency, repeated “capacity constrained” errors, support tickets referencing throttling.
- Goal: Fast triage; suggest Dedicated capacity, rate limit increases, batching/caching/throughput tuning; pull SE earlier.

C) Compliance / private deployment intent
- Examples: security/SOC2 FAQ views, VPC/private docs interest, SSO/SAML/KMS docs interest, retention controls questions.
- Goal: Route to AE+SE; offer security review + evidence pack; propose Dedicated/Private fit.

D) Team expansion / multi-workspace
- Examples: new workspaces, org invites spike, multiple API keys, multiple teams.
- Goal: Introduce account structuring, governance, consolidated billing; loop CS if already paying.

Ownership + handoffs (v1)
- If existing AE owner in HubSpot: preserve owner.
- If existing CSM owner + “existing customer expansion” tag: notify CSM + align on who sends first touch.
- If signal type = Compliance/Private OR Reliability high severity: add SE task same day (Markus Klein or regional SE pool).

Suppression rules (must check before Touch 1)
- If Marketing nurture email sent in last 48h for the same theme (Dedicated/Private/security): pause outbound 48h or coordinate copy.
- If customer has open support escalation (P1/P2) or active incident comms: do not pitch; convert to help-first touch.
- If account marked “Do not contact” OR prior complaint: stop.

HubSpot logging (required)
- Log Outcome on the PLG Signal Task: Meeting booked / No response / Not now / Disqualified / Already in motion.
- Add note: “Reason: <signal>” + “Next step: <CTA>” + “Suppression applied: Y/N”.


CADENCE: Day 0 / 2 / 5 / 10 (default)
- Touch 1: Day 0 (Email) + (optional) LinkedIn connect if persona is active.
- Touch 2: Day 2 (Call + VM) + short follow-up email.
- Touch 3: Day 5 (Email w/ resource + specific offer) + LinkedIn note.
- Touch 4: Day 10 (Breakup / close-the-loop email).

Target personas (pick 1–2 max)
- Developer lead / Eng manager (scale/reliability)
- Head of Platform / Infra (Dedicated, throughput)
- Security / Compliance (Private, retention, KMS)
- Product (expansion + roadmap alignment)

Variables (HubSpot template tokens)
- {{first_name}}, {{company}}, {{role}}, {{product_area}}
- {{signal_summary}} (one sentence, human-friendly)
- {{observed_symptom}} (e.g., rate limiting / growth)
- {{suggested_next_step}} (e.g., capacity review)
- {{calendar_link}} (AE link)
- {{security_pack_link}} (internal-approved doc)
- {{benchmark_offer}} (SE-led)


EMAIL TEMPLATES

Template 1 — Scale / spend velocity (Day 0)
Subject options:
- “Quick capacity + cost check for {{company}}?”
- “Scaling Redwood usage — want a 15-min throughput plan?”

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Noticed {{company}}’s Redwood usage has been trending up recently ({{signal_summary}}). Teams usually hit a point where they want more predictable throughput and clearer unit economics.

If it’s helpful, I can share a quick capacity + cost plan for your current workload (including what Dedicated would look like vs staying on Hosted, and a couple optimization levers).

Open to a 15-min chat this week? {{calendar_link}}

— {{sender_name}}

PS: If someone else owns infrastructure/performance for this, happy to loop them in.

[COMMENT - Ben Carter]: “Trending up” is good; avoid quoting exact spend in email. Use relative language unless they’ve asked.


Template 2 — Reliability / repeated 429s (Day 0)
Subject options:
- “Seeing throttling — can we help?”
- “Throughput / rate limits for {{company}}”

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Wanted to reach out because it looks like you may have run into throughput/rate limiting recently ({{signal_summary}}). If you’re scaling traffic, this is a common inflection point.

We can help in two ways:
1) Quick config review (batching/caching + limits) to reduce 429s without hurting latency
2) If you need guaranteed headroom, we can map your target TPS to Dedicated capacity

Want to do a 20-min triage with an SE on the line? {{calendar_link}}

— {{sender_name}}

[COMMENT - Markus Klein]: Add “we can look at request patterns” but do NOT imply we saw their prompts/content. Keep it about metrics.


Template 3 — Compliance / Private intent (Day 0)
Subject options:
- “Security review / deployment options for {{company}}”
- “VPC / Private deployment questions?”

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

If you’re evaluating Redwood for a security- or compliance-sensitive workload, happy to help. Many teams start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated or Private once requirements (SSO/SAML, audit logs, retention, KMS, data residency) are formalized.

We can do a 30-min security + deployment review and share the standard evidence pack (SOC 2, architecture overview, data handling notes).

Would a session this week be useful? {{calendar_link}}

— {{sender_name}}

[COMMENT - Dr. Aisha Rahman]: Don’t promise specific reports in the email. Say “evidence pack” and confirm availability per NDA/DPA process.


Template 4 — Team expansion / multi-workspace (Day 0)
Subject options:
- “Multi-team rollout for Redwood at {{company}}”
- “Governance + billing as teams adopt Redwood”

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Looks like Redwood usage at {{company}} may be expanding across multiple users/workspaces ({{signal_summary}}). When adoption spreads, teams often want a cleaner structure for governance (SSO, API key management), usage visibility, and consolidated billing.

Open to a quick call to understand how teams are using Redwood today and whether an account structure / Dedicated capacity would simplify things? {{calendar_link}}

— {{sender_name}}

[COMMENT - Jasmine Liu]: For paid customers, make sure CSM is aware before sending this. We don’t want two parallel “rollout” convos.


CALL TALK TRACK (Day 2)
Goal: Confirm the “why now,” offer help, and earn a meeting.

Opener (permission-based)
- “Hi {{first_name}}, this is {{sender_name}} from Redwood Inference. I’m reaching out because we noticed {{signal_summary}}. Did I catch you at an okay time for 30 seconds?”

If yes → frame
- “The reason I’m calling: teams often hit a scaling point where Hosted works, but they either want (a) more predictable throughput, (b) fewer rate limits / better tail latency, or (c) tighter security controls. I wanted to see what’s driving things on your side.”

Discovery prompts (pick 3)
Scale / economics
- “What’s driving the increase — a new feature launch or more customers?”
- “Do you have a target throughput (req/s or tokens/s) you need to hit reliably?”
- “How are you thinking about cost per request / per token for this feature?”

Reliability
- “Are 429s impacting users or just internal testing?”
- “What latency SLO do you need at p95/p99?”
- “Any peak windows where you need guaranteed headroom?”

Compliance
- “Any requirements around data residency, retention controls, audit logs, SSO/SAML, or KMS?”
- “Is this going through vendor security review now or later?”

Close (two-track CTA)
- “I can set up a 20–30 min session with an SE to map your target throughput + deployment requirements to a plan (Hosted optimizations vs Dedicated vs Private). Does {{two_time_options}} work?”

Voicemail (if no answer)
- “Hi {{first_name}}, {{sender_name}} at Redwood. Calling because it looks like {{company}} may be hitting {{observed_symptom}} recently. We can help reduce 429s / plan capacity. I’ll send a short email as well — feel free to grab time here: {{calendar_link}}.”

[COMMENT - Stephanie Nguyen]: For AEs, keep the call close short. Book meeting; don’t do full discovery live unless they engage.


FOLLOW-UP EMAIL SNIPPETS (Day 2 after call/VM)
Snippet A (after VM)
- “Just left you a quick VM. Happy to help with {{observed_symptom}} / capacity planning. If it’s easier, here’s my link: {{calendar_link}}.”

Snippet B (after live connect, meeting not booked)
- “Thanks for the quick chat. Based on what you said about {{key_need}}, I’d suggest we pull in an SE to map options (Hosted tuning vs Dedicated/Private). Does {{time_option_1}} or {{time_option_2}} work?”


DAY 5 EMAIL (value-add + specific offer)
Pick one asset/offering (do NOT attach large docs without asking).

Scale/reliability option:
Subject: “Throughput benchmark plan for {{company}}”
Body:
- “If you can share rough targets (avg/p95 tokens, concurrency), we can propose a benchmark plan and a capacity recommendation. If helpful, we’ll run it live with you.”

Compliance option:
Subject: “Security/deployment checklist (Hosted → Dedicated/Private)”
Body:
- “We have a standard checklist for vendor review (audit logs, retention, KMS, SSO, data residency). Happy to walk through it and identify what deployment mode fits.”

[COMMENT - Camila Reyes]: Ensure this doesn’t conflict with the lifecycle email that sends “Dedicated overview” on Day 3. We should either suppress the marketing email or align wording.


LINKEDIN PLACEHOLDERS
Connection note (short)
- “Hi {{first_name}} — I work with teams scaling LLM inference on Redwood. Reaching out because it looks like you may be scaling usage. Would love to connect.”

Follow-up note (after email)
- “Sharing here too in case it’s easier: happy to compare Hosted vs Dedicated/Private for your throughput/security needs.”

[COMMENT - Isabelle Laurent]: LinkedIn is optional; do not require in HubSpot task checklist. We’ll keep as “if appropriate.”


DAY 10 BREAKUP / CLOSE-THE-LOOP EMAIL
Subject options:
- “Close the loop?”
- “Should I stay in touch?”

Body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I haven’t heard back — totally fine. I reached out because {{signal_summary}} and we can usually help teams either (1) reduce throttling / improve tail latency or (2) plan predictable capacity (Dedicated/Private) when usage ramps.

If it’s not a priority right now, reply with “later” and I’ll circle back next month. If you’d rather not get these notes, tell me and I’ll close it out.

— {{sender_name}}


EXIT CRITERIA (stop the cadence)
Stop immediately if any of the below occurs:
- Meeting booked OR they reply with a clear next step.
- They reply “not now” with a timeframe → set a single follow-up task for that timeframe (no more steps).
- They request “no sales outreach” / complain about outreach → mark suppression + notify Ops.
- Account is already in an active sales cycle (open opp, mutual action plan) → switch to opp-driven communication.
- CS-owned expansion in progress and CSM asks to pause → defer to CS plan.

DISQUALIFICATION GUIDANCE (when to mark as false positive)
- The signal was caused by a load test / internal experiment / short-lived spike and they confirm no ongoing need.
- They’re a student/hobby project, no production intent.
- They’re already committed to a different vendor and only benchmarking.

What to say if they ask “How did you know?” (approved language)
- “We look at aggregate usage and reliability metrics in our platform to help customers scale successfully (e.g., rate limiting / throughput needs). We don’t see or use your prompt content for sales outreach.”

[COMMENT - Marcus Lin]: Keep this consistent with the data handling doc; avoid over-specific assurances if not formally stated there.


INTERNAL REVIEW NOTES / OPEN QUESTIONS
- Q: Should we run different cadences for trial vs paid?
  - Proposal: Trials get softer CTA + one fewer touch (Day 0/3/7) unless compliance intent is high.
- Q: Do we require SE on all reliability signals?
  - Proposal: Only if severity ≥ “High” (e.g., repeated 429s over multiple days) or if they mention production impact.
- Q: Who sends first touch for existing customers?
  - Proposal: CSM sends if account is tagged “existing customer expansion” and CSM is active; AE can co-sign on reply.

Change log
- v1 (2025-05-08): Initial draft from enablement sync.
- v1.1 (2025-05-15): Added compliance language + ‘How did you know?’ guidance.
- v1.2 (2025-05-28): Added suppression rules + reduced aggressive language per AE feedback.

Owner checklist before publishing (v1)
- Confirm Marketing suppression window (Tyler Benson + Camila Reyes)
- Confirm SE assignment rule in HubSpot workflow (Markus Klein + David Kim)
- Confirm CS handoff tags + notification (Jasmine Liu)
- Train AEs/SDRs on “How did you know?” response + logging outcomes
